problems.field: participants.n_randomized (and the rationale in participants.exclusions and reconciliation.agreed_fields_checked)
problems.form_value: null, because 'the paper gives no count stated at assignment'
problems.source_says: The paper states two counts at assignment, not none. Section 4 calls the randomized controlled experiment N = 502. Section 4.1 puts random assignment directly after consent, so the attention checks and the other exclusion reasons in Section 4.3 (AI use during the study, nonsense answers, repeat participation, unfinished questionnaire) all come after assignment. That supports 502 randomized and 486 analyzed. The Figure 1 caption instead says 'Participants (N = 486) were randomly assigned', and the abstract and p. 3 call the experiment N = 486. The form's own paper_design_summary reads 'a preregistered randomized experiment with 502 UK Prolific participants (486 analyzed)', which conflicts with null. Better coding: n_randomized = 502, with the Figure 1 and abstract wording noted. The per-arm n_randomized = null is right, because no per-arm exclusions are printed.
problems.quote: we performed a preregistered (https://aspredicted.org/nf5r-cmrt.pdf) randomized controlled experiment with N = 502 participants. ... After providing informed consent, participants were randomly assigned to one of the five experimental conditions.
problems.locator: PDF p. 5, Section 4 and Section 4.1; p. 7, Section 4.3; p. 2, Figure 1 caption; p. 1, Abstract; p. 3

problems.field: people analyzed (n_units null, no count or caveat recorded)
problems.form_value: null. measure_detail implies the analyzed question-mode, suggestion-mode, and model-led arms (Table 2: 96 + 95 + 101 = 292 people) and records t(295)
problems.source_says: The paper never prints how many people entered the within-subject model. It is a linear mixed model with participant random intercepts, three arms, and two ideas per person. With the 292 people of Table 2, within-person contrasts would carry about 292 - 3 = 289 df. The printed t(295) fits about 298 people. So S1-O3 may rest on a sample that differs from the 486 analyzed, by about 6 people. The form does not flag this. An S1-O3 record should not take its n from Table 2 without a note.
problems.quote: Whereas for the model-led (Δ = −0.09, 95% CI [−0.11, −0.07], t(295) = −9.80, p < .001) and suggestion-mode condition (Δ = −0.03, 95% CI [−0.04, −0.01], t(295) = −2.67, p = .006), diversity decreased significantly
problems.locator: PDF p. 9, Section 5.3; p. 24, Appendix G, Tables 12-13 (participant random intercepts); p. 12, Table 2

problems.field: contrasts[0].reported (number of coded ideas behind the elaboration-diversity correlation)
problems.form_value: 'Across coded ideas, elaboration depth correlated with idea diversity (r = 0.28, p = .032)'
problems.source_says: The paper coded 80 ideas (20 conversations in each of four AI arms) but does not say how many entered this correlation. With n = 80, r = 0.28 gives a two-sided p of about .012. The printed p = .032 fits about 60 ideas. So 'across coded ideas', read as all 80, is not supported. n_units = 80 for the descriptive percentages is right.
problems.quote: Results showed that deeper elaboration was associated with greater idea diversity (r = 0.28, p = .032), but not with quality or ownership (both p > .15).
problems.locator: PDF p. 9, Section 5.4 ('20 conversations per condition (80 ideas in total)'); p. 10, Section 5.4

confirmed.statement: Study 1 analyzed 486 people. The paper prints 502 recruited and removes 10 + 2 + 2 + 1 + 1 = 16 under its preregistered exclusion criteria. 502 - 16 = 486. The form's participants.n_analyzed (486) and its exclusions breakdown match.
confirmed.quote: Overall, N = 502 participants from the U.K. were recruited via the platform Prolific. ... This resulted in a final sample of N = 486 participants.

confirmed.statement: The Study 1 arm sizes, read on the PDF page, are question-mode 96, suggestion-mode 95, model-led 101, vanilla 95, and control 99. They sum to 486. The form's arm n_analyzed values match.
confirmed.quote: Question Mode 96 ... Suggestion Mode 95 ... Model-Led 101 ... Vanilla 95 ... Control 99

confirmed.statement: The Study 1 counts are people, not ideas or ratings. Each person has one scored idea, because raters judge only the first idea a person gives. Every H1 to H5 test has t(481) = 486 - 5, and the workload regression has F(1, 484) = 486 - 2, so each model has one row per person.
confirmed.quote: When one person provides several ideas: judge only the first one.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 22, Appendix D; p. 8, Section 5.1; p. 12, Table 3; p. 23, Table 11

confirmed.statement: No page gives per-arm exclusions or per-arm counts at assignment for Study 1. The 16 exclusions are not split by arm. The arm-level n_randomized = null is right.
confirmed.locator: Whole document read (markdown pp. 1-28, appendices included; PDF pages 1-16 and 22-28 viewed)

confirmed.statement: Study 1 assigned individuals at random after consent, so it is a randomized study of people.
confirmed.quote: After providing informed consent, participants were randomly assigned to one of the five experimental conditions.

confirmed.statement: Study 2 analyzed 640 people in six conditions. Its diversity and ownership tests have t(634) = 640 - 6, one row per person. The form's n_analyzed (640) and counts_are (people) match.
confirmed.quote: Our final sample in the validation study consisted of N = 640 participants across six conditions.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 11, Section 6.1; p. 12, Table 4; p. 26, Table 18

confirmed.statement: Study 2 gives no recruitment count, no exclusions, no per-arm sizes, no platform for the idea generators, and no statement of random assignment. The 320 Prolific student raters are raters and enter no people count. The form's nulls and 'not stated' entries for Study 2 are right.
confirmed.quote: we recruited N = 320 raters with active student status via Prolific (each rating 20 ideas).
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 10-13, Section 6; pp. 26-28, Appendix H.2 and Appendix I

confirmed.statement: The Study 2 population code general_public rests on the limitations section.
confirmed.quote: In addition, our participants were drawn from the general public

confirmed.statement: The two studies are separate samples. The paper adds them to a total of 1,126 (486 + 640). It does not say whether Study 1 participants could join Study 2, and it does not name Study 2's platform. The 50-person pilot only tested the system and is not analyzed.
confirmed.quote: we provide the first large-scale controlled experimental evaluation (total N = 1,126)

confirmed.statement: No other paper in the screening reuses these participants. candidates.json has no other record with this task, preregistration, or repository. c066 (Holzner, Maier, Feuerriegel 2025) is a meta-analysis with no data from this experiment, and c049 is a synthesis that cites the arXiv version. citations-family.json lists no sibling paper for c094.

confirmed.statement: The Study 1 'who' fields match p. 7 word for word: U.K., Prolific, the inclusion criteria, ages 18 to 78, M = 41.34, SD = 12.99 (the age figures also match Table 8). The gender shares do not reproduce exactly from 486 (239 women = 49.18 percent, 246 men = 50.62 percent) or from 502 (49.20 and 50.60 percent). confirmed.statement: Criterion 2 holds on Study 1 alone: 486 people analyzed, 95 to 101 per arm, in a design that randomizes individuals.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 5, Section 4.1; p. 7, Section 4.3; p. 12, Table 2

summary: Study 1's analyzed counts are right and count people (486 in total, with 96, 95, 101, 95, and 99 by arm), Study 2's 640 is right, and Study 1 alone has far more than 50 randomized people analyzed, so criterion 2 holds. The coding fails on details: Study 1 n_randomized is null although Section 4 gives the randomized experiment as N = 502 with 16 later exclusions (the form's own summary says so), and two exploratory analyses imply samples that differ from what the form implies (the S1-O3 t(295) fits about 298 people, not 292, and the S1-O4 r = .28 with p = .032 fits about 60 ideas, not 80), with no flag in the form.
